# routeros_ip_arp (Resource)


## Example Usage
```terraform
resource "routeros_ip_arp" "ap" {
  address     = "192.168.88.2"
  interface   = "bridge"
  mac_address = "02:00:00:00:00:02"
  comment     = "access point"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `address` (String) IP address to be mapped.
- `interface` (String) Interface name the IP address is assigned to.
- `mac_address` (String) MAC address to be mapped to.

### Optional

- `comment` (String)
- `disabled` (Boolean)
- `published` (Boolean) Static proxy-arp entry for individual IP address.

### Read-Only

- `complete` (Boolean) Whether the entry is resolved.
- `dhcp` (Boolean) Whether the entry was added by the DHCP server.
- `dynamic` (Boolean) Configuration item created by software, not by management interface. It is not exported, and cannot be directly modified.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `invalid` (Boolean)
- `status` (String) Neighbor state of the entry.
- `vrf` (String) The VRF table of the interface this address is assigned to.

## Import
Import is supported using the following syntax:
```shell
#The ID can be found via API or the terminal
#The command for the terminal is -> :put [/ip/arp get [print show-ids]]
terraform import routeros_ip_arp.ap "*1"
#Or you can import a resource using one of its attributes
terraform import routeros_ip_arp.ap "address=192.168.88.2"
```
